fieldValues.title: A meeting's raw transcript stays provenance; its important fragments become vignettes
fieldValues.move: Hold each recording's transcript as one attached file under one source record, the way other source files are held: a WebVTT file (W3C), one cue per spoken segment, cited by time with W3C Media Fragments (`<documentId>#t=a,b`). Pull the fragments that carry meaning out as vignettes that point back to the source and the time, and derive records only from those vignettes. A local detector proposes candidate fragments; a person picks them.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: It does not stop an export carrying the attached transcript: RFC-026 takes attached documents with any record that cites them (SP-124, srs#1002). It does not identify speakers, and whisper's base model mishears words, so a fragment still has to be checked against the audio. The live view during a meeting and the link from minutes to the transcript are a separate remedy (eeefe987, SP-158).
fieldValues.falsifier: People regularly need to search, comment on or link individual utterances, not fragments; or the detector's candidates miss fragments a person would have picked, so someone has to read the whole transcript anyway.
source_ref: srs-programme vignettes c26e0903 (the owner, 2026-11-05) and 965499aa (2026-11-09: one file, not plain text, small chunks, a basic transcription standard)
Trial 2026-11-05 on a 52-minute meeting: 808 utterance records and 1,643 files in a scratch repository, whole chain 11 minutes; the local detector gave 33 candidates in 3 minutes
Built 2026-11-09 (transcribe#3): the same meeting as one attached WebVTT file of 796 cues in 635 s, 0 validation errors
fieldValues.return_when: Individual utterances turn out to need their own relations or comments often enough to justify a record each.
